KEC International's Mali branch received an assessment order from the Directorate of Large Enterprise, Mali, raising a tax demand of Rs. 6.1 crore and penalty of Rs. 6.8 crore for January 2020 to December 2021.

news.headline:
The Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas has nominated Shri Rajeev Kumar, Deputy Director General (MoP&NG), as a Government Nominee Director on the Board of GAIL (India) Limited.

The tenure is for three years, on a co-terminus basis, or until further orders, whichever is earlier, with GAIL completing the requisite appointment formalities.

Source: BSE

news.headline:
L&T's Transportation Infrastructure vertical secured twin contracts from Dubai's Roads and Transport Authority (RTA) for the Latifa Bint Hamdan Corridor, categorized as one 'large' (Rs 2,500-5,000 Cr) and one 'significant' (Rs 1,000-2,500 Cr).

The project scope includes the construction of a new road, bridges, tunnels, Al Meydan interchange, and a cycling track, with completion scheduled by end-2028.

Source: ScoutQuest

news.headline:
Indo Gulf Industries shareholders approved the FY26 audited financial statements at its 43rd AGM. Members also approved the appointment and redesignation of Arjun Singh Bhandari as Managing Director for five years and the reappointment of Director Rajesh Jain.

Shareholders approved material related-party transactions for FY 2026–27 with Ganesh Explosives up to ₹17 crore and Rajesh Explosives up to ₹2 crore, and ratified the remuneration of cost auditors Gautam Chhetri & Co.

Source: BSE

news.headline:
Steel Strips Infrastructures held its 53rd Annual General Meeting on September 30, 2026, transacting key agenda items, including the adoption of FY26 financial statements and the re-appointment of retiring director Rajinder Kumar Garg.

The company also considered re-appointing Sanjay Garg as Managing Director for five years without remuneration and Humesh Kumar Singhal as Independent Director. Final voting results will be declared separately following the scrutinizer's report.

Source: BSE

news.headline:
In its 25th AGM transcript, VVIP Infratech reported a consolidated total income of ₹349.7 crore and PAT of ₹30.1 crore for FY 2025-26. Standalone total income reached ₹262.8 crore with a profit after tax of ₹22.7 crore.

The company maintains an order book of approximately ₹1,000 crore, driven by STP projects and a ₹198 crore Delhi sewerage tender, alongside steady expansion across residential and commercial developments in the NCR and Uttar Pradesh.

Source: BSE
